data.why: No real videos, SLEAP predictions, or trained model are bundled (the model is 'available on request'), so scripts/generate_demo_data.py synthesizes a tiny cohort (one Barnes video + two NOR videos) and matching SLEAP .predictions.slp files directly with sleap-io; the version shipped in the repo called PredictedInstance.from_numpy with keyword names (instance_score) that the pinned sleap-io release no longer accepts, so the seeded copy looks up the actual from_numpy signature at runtime and passes whichever point/score/instance-score keyword names it finds, then is run once during install to populate data/cohort_demo/ before Streamlit starts.

goals: Click the Barnes maze centre and target hole once on a reference frame and save the cohort geometry
Calibrate the two NOR object positions on a familiar-phase frame, then mark which side held the novel object on a test-phase video
Run the cleaning + validation + metrics pipeline on a cohort and watch the live step-by-step progress log
Inspect the data-quality banner for videos flagged with long nose/tail tracking blackouts before trusting their metrics
Read off per-video Barnes metrics (latency to target, time at target, target-quadrant occupancy) and NOR metrics (discrimination index, exploration time) and export them as CSV
Plot a video's cleaned nose trajectory, colour-coded by frame number, to sanity-check the tracking

review.summary: The goal and the first three phases (setup, calibrating Barnes and NOR, labelling the novel side) match the README, and their screens check out. But every pipeline run crashed on what looks like a sleap-io version mismatch, so the tree has no metrics, quality-flag, trajectory or export tasks, which is what the tool is for. Fix the environment, re-run the review phase, and trim the one-click tasks before filing.
